question: Using Section 4I.06 and Figure 4I-4, describe the pedestrian interval order, minimum buffer interval, and walking speed normally used for clearance timing.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Section 4I.06 and Figure 4I-4, the pedestrian intervals occur in this order: a Walk Interval (steady WALKING PERSON, 7 seconds minimum, reducible under some conditions), followed immediately by a Pedestrian Change Interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND, with an optional countdown display), followed by a Buffer Interval (steady UPRAISED HAND) of at least 2 seconds before conflicting traffic is released. The Buffer Interval must always be provided and displayed. The pedestrian clearance time is normally timed using a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second, with a slower speed considered where slower pedestrians or wheelchair users routinely cross. Standards (mandatory): - Per the Figure 4I-4 note: "The Buffer Interval, which shall always be provided and displayed, may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended." - The full-page views of the Section 4I.06 Standard text further show that the buffer interval, consisting of a steady UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK), shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement, and that the sum of the pedestrian change interval and buffer interval shall not be less than the calculated pedestrian clearance time [Image 6]. Guidance (recommended): - "Except as provided in Paragraph 8 of this Section, the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait." - "Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time." Options (permitted): - "The additional time provided by an extended push button press to satisfy pedestrian clearance time needs may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval." - Per the Figure 4I-4 notes: the countdown display is optional for Pedestrian Change Intervals of 7 seconds or less, and the Buffer Interval may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time or may begin after the calculated clearance time has ended. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 shows the interval sequence — steady UPRAISED HAND, Walk Interval (steady WALKING PERSON, "7 seconds MIN."), Pedestrian Change Interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND with countdown), and Buffer Interval (steady UPRAISED HAND, "2 seconds MIN.") — along with the "zero" point of the countdown display and five possible relationships between the buffer interval and vehicular yellow/red clearance intervals. - [Image 5] The full page containing Figure 4I-4 also shows the Guidance text specifying the 3.5 feet per second walking speed and the note that the Buffer Interval shall always be provided and displayed. - [Image 6] The full page containing Figure 4I-3 shows the Standard that the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND) shall begin immediately after the WALKING PERSON indication, followed by a buffer interval displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Guidance §7 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §10 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Support §6 (p.724) - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Page 765 - Page 764
gold_answer: The order is WALK, flashing DONT WALK pedestrian change interval, then steady DONT WALK buffer interval. The buffer interval is at least 2 seconds before conflicting traffic is released, and clearance is normally evaluated using 3.5 feet per second.
